stemMd: After a carbohydrate-rich meal, blood glucose rises. Which response normally helps lower it?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Increased insulin secretion promoting glucose uptake and storage

options.label: B
options.textMd: Increased glucose release with no compensating uptake

options.label: D
options.textMd: Release of bile directly into blood to digest glucose

options.label: E
options.textMd: Conversion of all plasma proteins into glucose

explanationMd: Insulin promotes uptake and storage of glucose in responsive tissues. The response counteracts the initial rise, illustrating negative feedback rather than amplification of the disturbance.

distractorRationale.c: This would impair the normal corrective response.
distractorRationale.b: This would tend to raise blood glucose.
distractorRationale.d: Bile acts in the intestine and does not digest glucose.
distractorRationale.e: This would not explain glucose lowering.
